extra_snippets: Citi has agreed to acquire Kard Financial, expanding its customer engagement, rewards, and commerce media capabilities as the bank looks to deliver more personalized offers across its massive U.S. cardholder base. Kard operates a commerce media and rewards platform that helps banks, fintechs, and neobanks connect customers with personalized merchant-funded offers. The company uses verified transaction data, machine learning-powered personalization, and matching technology to help financial institutions deliver more relevant rewards while giving merchants and brands a way to reach consumers who are already demonstrating purchasing intent.

Kard’s model is designed around merchant-funded rewards, meaning participating brands and merchants can fund incentives that are delivered through financial institutions and fintech platforms. The company also uses machine learning to help determine which offers are most relevant to particular customers, simplifying the process for issuers while potentially improving engagement and redemption.

Until the transaction closes, Citi and Kard will continue operating as independent organizations. The acquisition remains subject to customary closing conditions. Support: Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, a Stifel company, served as exclusive financial advisor to Kard.
Citi plans to combine its scale, payments infrastructure, and customer relationships with Kard’s technology, merchant network, and personalization capabilities.

For Kard, the agreement would place its technology inside a much larger banking platform.

Kard's platform is built around transaction-level data and automated matching of offers to likely buyers. The model is designed to help financial institutions present rewards in a more tailored way while giving merchants clearer information on whether an offer led to a purchase. The approach has become more relevant as banks, payment companies and retailers look for new ways to use spending data to improve customer engagement and generate advertising income from commerce activity.
Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, a Stifel company, acted as exclusive financial adviser to Kard, while Sullivan & Cromwell advised Citi and Latham & Watkins advised Kard.
